title: Everything that worked before the Wave 5 merge (#95) still works after it
baseline: 9b28a1c (main, merge of #94; same tree as 2fe8144) compared with 53bdb1f (dev after #95)

checks.what: OpenAPI request contract of every released /api operation, old vs new: removed operation, parameter, body or field, narrowed type, new requirement, tighter limit, closed object (214 released operations, 36 added)

Committed contract snapshot test (tests/test_openapi_regression.py + tests/openapi_snapshot.json): fails CI on an incompatible change, allows additions; proven with a real removed field and narrowed type
Response shapes, old vs new on the same data: 44 parameterless GETs, every store read route, the waited Path analyzer (hops matched by key); only additions

_tenant_creds cloud fallback: 26,784 cases (every request model x body cloud x typed identity x profile x environment x tenant_config.json), old vs new; identical whenever the body names a cloud and whenever no source names one; differences only where a fallback source names the cloud (the intended fix)

The pre-Wave-5 test suite run against the post-Wave-5 code: 8128 passed, 16 failed, every failure explained by a deliberate #95 edit of that test or its data (new routes in route tables, new scripts and toolbar button, wording allow-list, XSS allow-list entries, additive access key, release workflow)
Rule migration end to end over HTTP on a stateful fake: status, fetch, analyze, plan, export JSON/CSV, post dry run, refused without each gate, applied in the planned order
Remediation (one-click fixes): catalog, plan, dry run, refused without write mode or confirmation, then exactly the planned call
Pack deploy through the gates, deployment record, undo back to the starting tenant; removal preview and removal through the gates

MCP server: four tools over the MCP tool API on a fake; full 206-check engine run old vs new identical except the intended Client Connector numeric device-state fix (old code raised on an integer state)
Browser extension side-panel calls from its own origin: ping, profiles, console index, notes, export job, poll and download

Assessment run, export from tenant, self-heal, change queue, HAR batch, Simple mode wizards, Word/PDF/Excel exports: existing end-to-end HTTP tests confirmed (test_assess_stream, test_pack_export, test_self_heal, test_team_queue, test_har_import, test_simple_mode, test_exports_excel_pdf, test_export_integrity); report_docx/report_exports changes are additive

Data migration: profiles (remembered secret, classic sign-in, history with and without per-check states), proposals, change queue, workspace notes, posture settings, deployments, bulk changes and self-heal state written by the pre-Wave-5 code (tools/pre_wave5_fixtures.py) load, resolve the same sign-in and keep their content when changed
Damaged store files, old vs new: identical outcome for every variant except a non-object snapshots entry (new 500)
Log analyzer PAC reading over a corpus of ten PAC styles, old vs new: answers, default, gateways, bypass inventory and findings
Path analyzer destination acceptance, old parse vs new parse plus traffic check over 30 destinations
Determinism: full suite in normal order and in a seeded shuffle of modules and tests (scratch plugin, seed 6095), plus a final reverse-order run; threads alive at each test start logged
Known flake test_tenant_pacing: root cause found and removed

findings.title: Log analyzer: a PAC the new evaluator refuses (regular expression, array, loop, switch) lost its whole reading (default, gateways, bypass inventory, fail-open/closed, hard-coded gateway), including a reference-style PAC
findings.fix: log_analyzer reads such a PAC from its text again (never run, bounded to pac_eval.MAX_SOURCE) and still says it was not evaluated

findings.title: Log analyzer: a DIRECT condition written in a PAC helper function (isCorp(host)) was no longer listed as a bypass
findings.fix: pac_eval.inspect expands a helper's returned conditions once per condition (static, never run; recursion cannot loop)

findings.title: Tenant profiles: a store whose snapshots entry is not an object made the profile list and profile delete fail with 500 (the pre-Wave-5 code ignored the key)
findings.fix: tenant_profiles._read treats a non-object snapshots entry as empty

findings.title: Known flaky test_tenant_pacing: the 429-hold test asserted 19 s left of a 20 s hold on the wall clock, so a 1 s scheduling stall under load failed it (reproduced by injecting a 1.2 s stall)
findings.fix: the test freezes ZIA's rate clock at the moment the hold is published and asserts the exact 20 s

notes: /api/path-analyzer/full/start is not on dev or main; it is listed as unreleased in the snapshot test and will not be held to a contract until it ships.
OpenAPI declares no response models, so response compatibility is checked by live answers (top-level keys of 28 local read endpoints in the snapshot) rather than by schema.

Upper-bound timing assertions remain elsewhere (test_readiness huge-token < 0.5 s, test_flow_scenario_evidence < 2 s, test_zpa_analysis < 2 s); none failed in three full runs, so they are not changed.
A profile store hand-edited so that profiles is a list or a profile is a string gives 500 in both the old and the new code; no version writes that shape.
tests/test_assess_stream.py leaves a deliberately stuck check thread sleeping 30 s after its test; it touches no shared clock or state.
